what: the same probe on the build Microchip ships: data cache ON (Config.K0 = 3), interrupts masked, 10 500 traces

victim.stack: Microchip Harmony 3 net_apps_pic32mz snmpv3_nvm_mpfs on FreeRTOS, wolfCrypt AES with WOLFSSL_AES_SMALL_TABLES
victim.build: the shipped one: Config.K0 = 3 from XC32's crt0, and PRECON.PREFEN = 3 with PFMWS = 3 written by Harmony's own SYS_Initialize

geometry.note: same geometry as the cache-off vector, scored the same way, because a control has to fail at the attack's own settings.

attack.expect_note: no key: with the cache on there is nothing at the call to lose
attack.note: This vector is shallower than the one it controls - 10 500 traces against 60 000 - and the IV runs make the distinct-input count lower still, so read it as what it is. The claim it carries is not 'a 60 000-trace recovery failed'; it is that the AES call takes 11 distinct values across the whole capture, 83 percent of them identical, and that between-input variation (1.94 cycles) is SMALLER than same-input variation (4.12). There is no data dependence to swamp. Pooled z over the adjacent pairs is -0.56.

truth.note: the same victim and the same key as the cache-off vector, so the two differ in one flash-controller field.
